html:
The Wayilwan are an Aboriginal people of central northern New South Wales, in country around the Macquarie Marshes and the lower Castlereagh River. They are a group of the Ngiyampaa nation.

The Macquarie Marshes, a large wetland, gave fish, waterbirds and eggs. Neighbours on the map were the Gamilaraay to the east, the Wiradjuri to the south and the Wongaibon to the west.

Explorers such as John Oxley and Charles Sturt reached the marshes in 1818 and 1828, and squatters followed with sheep and cattle in the 1830s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
